objectives: Understand how home fellowships serve both discipleship and evangelism
Lead systematic Bible study that grounds believers in the whole Word
Organise home fellowships to care for members and reach neighbourhoods

modules.title: Word-centred growth
modules.summary: The power of systematic Bible study.

lessons.title: From a Bible study to a movement
lessons.body:
William Kumuyi began holding a weekly Bible study in Lagos in 1973 with a handful of university students. The focus was simple: study the Bible carefully and obey it, especially its call to repentance and holiness. As people were converted and grew, the study became the Deeper Christian Life Ministry and then the Deeper Life Bible Church, with congregations across Nigeria and many other nations.

That history illustrates biblical principles:

- **The Word builds believers**: Scripture is "profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness" (2 Timothy 3:16).
- **Searching the Scriptures** produces stable faith (Acts 17:11).
- **Regular teaching multiplies**: Paul's daily teaching in Ephesus reached all Asia (Acts 19:10).

Systematic Bible study (working through books and doctrines in order, with questions and memory verses) gives believers roots that sermons alone often cannot.

lessons.title: Leading a systematic Bible study
lessons.body:
Ezra's helpers "read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand" (Nehemiah 8:8). Jesus explained "in all the scriptures the things concerning himself" (Luke 24:27).

A study outline (like the weekly outlines many churches use) usually includes:

- **Topic and key text**.
- **Memory verse**.
- **Introduction**: why this matters.
- **Main points**, each with Bible references to look up.
- **Questions** for discussion.
- **Application**: what we will do.
- **Prayer points**.

Leading it:

- **Prepare** by studying the passage and the outline early.
- **Let members read** the references aloud.
- **Ask questions**; let people discover.
- **Keep to the text**; avoid side debates.
- **Apply** specifically: "be ye doers of the word" (James 1:22).
- **Review** memory verses each week.

quiz.q: How did the Deeper Life Bible Church begin?
options: As a weekly Bible study in Lagos in 1973
As a crusade in a stadium

quiz.q: What does 2 Timothy 3:16 say Scripture is profitable for?
options: Doctrine, reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness
Working through books and doctrines in order with questions and memory verses

quiz.q: Why let members read references aloud?
options: So they engage with the text themselves

lessons.title: Caring in homes
lessons.body:
Paul taught "publickly, and from house to house" (Acts 20:20). The early church met "from house to house... with gladness and singleness of heart" (Acts 2:46).

Home fellowships meet weekly in members' homes, grouped by neighbourhood. Their focus is **care**:

- **Knowing** each member and family by name.
- **Praying** for one another's needs.
- **Visiting** the sick, bereaved and absent.
- **Practical help**: food, rent support, job leads, school fees, within wisdom and the church's welfare structures.
- **Encouraging** holiness and growth.
- **Celebrating** together.

"Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love... Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep" (Romans 12:10, 15).

A fellowship leader should know the state of each member, like a shepherd who counts his sheep.

lessons.title: Reaching the neighbourhood
lessons.body:
"Ye are the light of the world... Let your light so shine before men" (Matthew 5:14, 16). A home fellowship is a light on a street.

Neighbourhood evangelism through home fellowships:

- **Pray** for every house on your street by name.
- **Invite** neighbours to an open fellowship evening with simple refreshments.
- **Hold occasional evangelistic meetings** in the home with a clear gospel message.
- **Serve** visibly: help in emergencies, clean-up days, care for the elderly.
- **Follow up** visitors within a week.
- **Bring whole households**: the jailer "believed in God with all his house" (Acts 16:34).
- **Connect** new believers to the church's new converts' class.

Many people who would never attend a church building will enter a neighbour's living room.

quiz.q: How did Paul teach in Ephesus, according to Acts 20:20?
options: Publicly and from house to house

quiz.q: What is the main focus of a home caring fellowship?
options: Care for members in their neighbourhood

quiz.q: Why are home fellowships effective for evangelism?
options: Many people who won't attend a church will enter a neighbour's home

quiz.q: What happened to the jailer's household in Acts 16:34?
options: They believed in God with all the house

lessons.title: Structure and reporting
lessons.body:
Moses appointed "rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens" (Exodus 18:21). Large churches stay caring by organising in small units with leaders who report upward.

A simple structure:

- **Fellowship leader** for each home group (with an assistant).
- **Zone or area coordinator** over several groups.
- **Church pastor or coordinator** over the zones.

Weekly or monthly **reports** (attendance, visitors, new converts, needs, prayer requests) help leaders know "the state of thy flocks" (Proverbs 27:23) and respond quickly to problems.

Keep reporting **simple**, use it to **serve people** (not to pressure leaders), and protect confidential information.

lessons.title: Training leaders and multiplying
lessons.body:
Groups multiply only when leaders are trained.

- **Choose** faithful, mature members (Acts 6:3).
- **Train** them regularly: Bible study methods, pastoral care, evangelism, handling problems.
- **Apprentice**: each leader trains an assistant who leads parts of meetings.
- **Equip** with study outlines and resources.
- **Multiply** when groups become too large (about 12 to 15 regular adults): the assistant leads a new group nearby.
- **Pray** for and care for leaders; visit them.

Kumuyi's ministry is known for regular, systematic training of workers so that growth is supported by teaching. Without trained leaders, growth becomes crowds without care.

quiz.q: What did Moses appoint in Exodus 18:21?
options: Rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens

quiz.q: What is the purpose of reports in home fellowships?
options: To help leaders know the state of the flock and respond to needs

quiz.q: When should a home fellowship multiply?
options: When it becomes too large, around 12 to 15 regular adults

quiz.q: What happens to growth without trained leaders?

final.q: What emphasis marked Kumuyi's early Bible study?
options: Careful Bible study and obedience, especially repentance and holiness

final.q: Which verse describes the Bereans searching the Scriptures daily?
Which element belongs in a Bible study outline?

options: Be doers of the word, not hearers only

final.q: Which is part of caring in a home fellowship?
options: Visiting the sick, bereaved and absent

final.q: Why pray for every house on your street by name?
options: To prepare the neighbourhood for the gospel

final.q: When should visitors be followed up?
Who oversees several home fellowship groups?
What should leaders do with confidential information in reports?
What does an apprentice leader do?
options: Leads parts of meetings and prepares to lead a new group

title: Home Caring Fellowships and Bible Study Groups
summary: Use home fellowships and systematic Bible study to disciple believers and reach neighbours, following a model that has helped churches grow across Nigeria.
about: The Deeper Christian Life Ministry, founded by William Kumuyi, grew from a weekly Bible study into one of Africa's largest churches, with home caring fellowships meeting in neighbourhoods and systematic Bible study at the heart of its life. This course draws on that experience and on Scripture to show how small home groups and structured Bible study can both disciple believers and reach the unsaved, and how to lead them faithfully.
audience: House fellowship and home cell leaders, Bible study leaders, church workers and evangelism coordinators.
prerequisites: How to Study the Bible is recommended.
outcomes: Describe the biblical and historical basis for home-based discipleship
Lead a Bible study using a structured outline with questions and applications
Plan neighbourhood outreach through a home fellowship
Set up a simple leadership and reporting structure

assignment.title: Practical assignment: a home fellowship plan
assignment.body:
Hand in (500 to 800 words):

1. A Bible study outline for one session (topic, key text, memory verse, points with references, questions, application, prayer points).
2. A plan for caring for members of a home fellowship.
3. A neighbourhood outreach plan for one street or estate.
4. A simple structure and reporting form.

If possible, lead one study and add a 150-word reflection.

reading: Carl George, Prepare Your Church for the Future
